column1: # LAB-ONLY. HELD ROWS of the INVIOLABLE workload rule (validation/wl_verdict.py; WL-DYNAMIC-GATE, owner ruling #6965,
# 2026-11-20; D-X.141). The rule binds the dynamic kit: each workload at or below 1.10x glibc in instructions:u and in
# page faults, geomean of instructions:u at or below 1.00. A row here was over 1.10x when the rule moved to the
# dynamic kit, for the cause it names; it is bounded at `level` (libniji / glibc, the ratio recorded on next, rounded
# up to 4 decimals) instead of 1.10. A RATCHET: a level is never raised and a row is never added for a CPU class
# already recorded (wl_verdict.py holds, run by validation/wl_verdict_test.sh against the merge base). A row that
# measures at or below 1.10x drops its hold in that run (HOLD-RELEASE): remove it (wl_verdict.py check --update).
# cpu = /proc/cpuinfo "model name" of the count host (instructions follow the IFUNC variant a CPU selects); glibc and
# libniji = the recorded counts, the WORST observed so a rerun of next does not exceed the level (a level a rerun can
# exceed is a flake), from a wl_count run whose BASE column is next: instructions:u the base column's mean and glibc's
# mean; page faults the highest single base run and the lowest glibc run (the log's "faults min..max" line); recorded =
# the measured next head and date.
